quality_assessment: Chapter covers the basics well but is missing several important features and edge cases that users may encounter

issues.description: The --no-context-separator flag is not documented, but exists in the codebase
issues.should_add: Document --no-context-separator flag which completely disables context separators (including line breaks)
issues.fix_suggestion: Add subsection explaining --no-context-separator as an alternative to empty string separator. Explain the difference: empty string still adds line breaks, --no-context-separator removes them completely.

issues.description: Field separators for context lines are not documented
issues.should_add: Document --field-context-separator which controls the separator between line number and context line content (default is '-')
issues.fix_suggestion: Add explanation that context lines use '-' as field separator while matching lines use ':'. Mention --field-context-separator and --field-match-separator flags for customization.

issues.description: Escape sequences in context separator are not demonstrated with examples
issues.current_content: The chapter mentions escape sequences can be used but shows no examples
issues.should_add: Show example using escape sequences like \x7F or \t in context separator

issues.description: The --passthru flag and its interaction with context flags is not explained
issues.should_add: Explain that --passthru shows ALL lines from files with matches, and context flags override --passthru
issues.fix_suggestion: Add section 'Context vs Passthru' explaining --passthru behavior and how -A/-B/-C override it

issues.description: The chapter mentions overlapping context but doesn't explain the behavior clearly
issues.current_content: When matches are close together, their context may overlap. ripgrep handles this gracefully by not duplicating lines.
issues.should_be: When matches are close together and their context windows overlap, ripgrep merges them into a single contiguous block without duplicating lines or adding separators between them.
issues.fix_suggestion: Expand explanation with a concrete example showing two matches 3 lines apart with -C 2, demonstrating how the overlapping context is merged

issues.description: The chapter suggests combining with --heading but doesn't explain what this does
issues.current_content: - Combine with `--heading` for clearer file organization
issues.should_be: Explain that --heading groups matches by filename (printed once as a header) instead of repeating filename on each line, which makes context blocks easier to read in multi-file searches
issues.fix_suggestion: Expand best practice to explain --heading mode and show a before/after example of context output with and without --heading

issues.description: No example showing how context separators can be completely disabled
issues.fix_suggestion: Add Example 5: Disabling Context Separators - Show search with --no-context-separator to remove all separation between match groups

positive_aspects: Clear, logical structure progressing from basic to advanced usage
Good coverage of -A/-B/-C flags with both short and long forms
Helpful examples showing practical use cases
Good explanation of line number display format differences (: vs -)
improvement_suggestions: Add visual examples showing actual output for each flag combination
Include example showing overlapping context behavior with concrete line numbers
Add section on context with --heading mode showing the visual difference
Show more examples of custom separators including escape sequences
Add example demonstrating field separator customization
Consider adding a reference table summarizing all context-related flags
Add cross-references to output-formats chapter for related formatting options

metadata.validation_focus: Ensure -A/-B/-C flags and context separator options are explained with examples
